analysis.title: ARM Holdings (ARM): Results above the Street, with positive AGI CPU commentary but royalty miss
key_insights: ARM reported FY2Q27 revenue of $1.44bn vs GS $1.39bn and Street (Visible Alpha) $1.38bn. Operating margin was 44.2% vs GS 42.2% and Street 41.6%. Operating EPS excl. SBC was $0.52 vs $0.48 for both GS and the Street.

Licensing and other revenue rose 50% YoY to a record $773mn, about $100mn above management expectations, vs GS $677mn and Street $667mn. Management cited accelerating customer demand for long-term access to ARM technology.

Royalty revenue was $670mn, about 5% below GS ($707mn) and Street ($708mn). Strength in Cloud AI and Physical AI was more than offset by weakness in Edge AI, as higher memory pricing weighs on smartphone demand.
Management expects smartphone headwinds to persist near-term and guided to low-single-digit YoY royalty growth in FY3Q (December).

Management's confidence in up to $2bn of AGI CPU revenue across FY27-FY28 has increased over the past 90 days. Purchase orders are secured from multiple customers, with first commercial deliveries on track for FY4Q27. The company is adding capacity.

Licensing added three new ARM Total Access agreements, taking active subscriptions above 60, including a first-time ATA with a major customer. It also signed four new compute subsystem licenses across data center and smartphones.

FY3Q27 guidance: revenue midpoint $1.54bn (range $1.49-1.59bn) vs GS $1.57bn and Street $1.52bn. Operating expense $825mn vs GS $811mn and Street $823mn. EPS midpoint $0.56 vs GS $0.60 and Street $0.55.
GS expects the stock to be range bound after the print. It says investor expectations were relatively balanced, with positive sentiment on the datacenter CPU ramp offset by the recent sector selloff.

GS keeps a Sell rating and $160 12-month price target (unchanged), based on 50x normalized EPS of $3.20, vs a $191.80 price (16.6% downside to target). Its concerns are near-term royalty pressure, no clear competitive advantage in chip manufacturing relative to peers, and elevated valuation.
GS says it could turn more constructive on evidence of an acceleration in royalty growth or more visibility into greater scale in chip manufacturing.

GS raised EPS estimates by about 1% on average, driven by higher Licensing and CPU silicon revenue, partly offset by lower Royalty revenue and lower gross margin assumptions. FY28E CPU revenue rose to $1,500mn from $1,000mn.

market_movers.rationale: Royalty revenue missed again on smartphone weakness, and GS sees no clear competitive advantage in chip manufacturing and an elevated valuation. The Sell is kept despite the licensing beat and stronger AGI CPU demand.

earnings_insights: ARM FY2Q27 (reported 11/4): revenue $1.44bn actual vs GS est $1.39bn and Street (Visible Alpha) est $1.38bn. Operating EPS excl. SBC $0.52 actual vs GS and Street est $0.48. Operating margin excl. SBC 44.2% actual vs GS est 42.2% and Street est 41.6%.

ARM FY2Q27 Licensing and other revenue $773mn actual (+50% YoY) vs GS est $677mn and Street est $667mn. Royalty revenue $670mn actual vs GS est $707mn and Street est $708mn. Gross margin excl. SBC was 97.9% actual vs GS est 98.6% and Street est 98.2%.

ARM FY3Q27 company guidance (December quarter): revenue midpoint $1.54bn, operating expense $825mn excl. SBC, EPS excl. SBC midpoint $0.56. GS est: revenue $1.57bn, EPS $0.60. Street est: revenue $1.52bn, EPS $0.55. Royalty revenue is guided to low-single-digit YoY growth.

GS revised estimates (EPS excl. SBC): FY2027E $2.26 (old $2.25), FY2028E $3.00 (old $2.95), FY2029E $3.80 (old $3.75). GS revenue: FY2027E $6,173mn (old $6,086mn), FY2028E $8,674mn (old $8,010mn), FY2029E $10,458mn (old $10,091mn).
GS FY2028E CPU revenue is $1,500mn (old $1,000mn) and FY2029E is $2,200mn (old $2,000mn). GS FY2028E gross margin is 87.1% (old 90.9%).
risk_factors: Royalty revenue is under near-term pressure from smartphone weakness, with higher memory pricing weighing on demand and management expecting the headwinds to persist.
Valuation is elevated relative to peers at about 85x GS FY2027E EPS, and GS sees no clear competitive advantage in chip manufacturing.
Upside risks to the Sell: a stronger datacenter ramp, better operating leverage, and better execution on chip manufacturing.
